I graded submission s1 for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s1.json`. You got 2 correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Wrong (M4) | The model can't open the booking system. It writes a request for `check_calendar`, and the program runs it. |
| q3 | Correct | A step limit is the right safeguard against a stuck loop. |
| q4 | Wrong (M4) | The answer is 4, not 1. The program runs each tool, and each result needs a new model call: 3 tool requests plus the final answer. |
| q5 | Partial | "Sends it back to the model" is right, but you left out why. The model needs the result in its next input to choose its next step or write the answer. |
| q6 | Partial (M3) | Tools are described to the model by name and description, which you had right. But the model doesn't remember earlier sessions on its own. The program has to supply that. |

The main thing to fix is who does what. The model only writes requests, and the program runs every tool. Your plan to track each student's training status will need the program to save that status and put it in the model's input.

**Next step:** re-trace the laser-cutter request on paper. For each step, write whether the model or the program acts, and what the model sees in that call. Then we can move on to context and memory.

I also wrote learning record `0003-model-requests-program-runs.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. I didn't grade `submissions/s2.json` because you only asked for s1. Do you want me to grade it next, to see whether the M4 and M3 mix-ups have cleared up?
